overview: White skips the usual 2.d4 and prepares a queenside bishop fianchetto with b3 and Bb2, aiming for a Larsen-style set-up. After 2...d5 3.Bb2 Black can play ...Nf6 or ...dxe4 or ...c5, and White tries to use the long diagonal against e5/g7. It is an uncommon way to avoid main-line French theory.

white_ideas.idea: Bb2, Nf3 and e5 or exd5 with long-diagonal pressure.
Delay d4 and see how Black sets up.

black_ideas.idea: ...d5 and ...Nf6, then ...c5 to strike the centre.
Take on e4 with ...dxe4 and keep the pawn or hit the b2 bishop with ...Bb4.

typical_structures.structure: French-type e6/d5 pawns against e4 with a bishop on b2, centre not yet settled.

character.notes: Quiet and slightly offbeat set-up; no forcing main line, though ...dxe4 gambit lines exist.

gambit.notes: Not in the main line; 3...dxe4 with Papa-Ticulat ideas is a sideline.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black comfortable equality; not refuted.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom use it; chosen to avoid theory.

level.notes: Few forced lines and clear plans.

sublines_that_differ.name: Papa-Ticulat Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: Listed in the database as the most played continuation and tied to a gambit try.

character.reason: Slow flank-style set-up that is neither forcing nor especially solid.

gambit.reason: No material is given in the main line.

soundness.reason: No refutation, just a risk-free but toothless sideline.

structure.reason: Centre undecided in a French-meets-flank-opening set-up.

plans.reason: Bb2 on the long diagonal is the point of the move.
